lessons.title: Bonjour, mes amis!
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize and respond to basic French greetings through gestures and visual cues

opening.activity: Gentle introduction with puppet saying 'Bonjour!' and waving. Show friendly face pictures of children greeting each other.
opening.visualSupports: Big wave gesture for 'bonjour', hand to heart for 'merci', wave goodbye for 'au revoir'

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves semblent-ils prêts pour cette première expérience en français?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Continuer avec enthousiasme et gestes accueillants
decisionPoints.ifNo: Ralentir le rythme et utiliser plus de sourires rassurants

main.activity: Circle time with greeting song using gestures. Pass the puppet around for each child to hear 'Bonjour [name]!' Practice greeting responses with thumbs up, wave, or smile.
main.visualSupports: Exaggerated facial expressions, large gesture demonstrations, picture sequence cards showing greeting interactions

decisionPoints.question: How comfortable are students with new French sounds?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Continue with puppet conversations and encourage verbal responses with 'Bonjour' attempts
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on gestures and visual responses, extend listening time with more repetition

decisionPoints.question: What level of gestures/TPR support is needed?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use full body movements and exaggerated gestures for kinesthetic learners
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use simple hand gestures and facial expressions for focused attention

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for individual greeting practice?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have puppet greet each child individually with their name
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep greetings as whole group activity with shared responses

closing.activity: Goodbye circle with puppet saying 'Au revoir!' to each child. Practice waving and saying goodbye.
closing.visualSupports: Large waving motion, 'Au revoir' lip formation, happy goodbye expressions

decisionPoints.question: Comment les élèves se sentent-ils après leur première leçon de français?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Célébrer leur succès et encourager leur retour
decisionPoints.ifNo: Rassurer avec des gestes doux et de la patience

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students seem overwhelmed by new sounds
troubleshooting.then: Use more gestures, slower pace, and focus on just 'bonjour' with lots of repetition

lessons.realWorldConnection: How people greet each other in French-speaking communities around the world

forStruggling: Use simple gestures only (wave, smile)
Allow non-verbal responses (pointing, nodding)
Provide extra visual cues and slower pace
Practice with puppet one-on-one if needed
forAdvanced: Encourage full French greetings 'Bonjour madame/monsieur'
Add time of day greetings 'Bon matin'
Practice greeting puppet in different voices
Help demonstrate for classmates
forELL: Connect to greetings in home language first
Use visual greeting sequence cards
Allow code-switching during learning phase
Focus on gesture recognition before speech
forIEP: Adapt to individual communication methods
Use assistive technology if needed
Allow extended processing time
Modify physical gestures as needed

observable: Student responds to 'Bonjour' with gesture or smile
Student shows recognition of French greeting sounds
Student demonstrates appropriate social greeting behavior
Student engages with puppet interaction positively
checkpoints: Can recognize 'Bonjour' when spoken
Attempts to wave or gesture in response
Shows comfort with French classroom environment
Participates in group greeting activities

lessons.title: Je m'appelle...
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand name introductions and begin to share their names using gestures and visual supports

opening.activity: Review 'Bonjour!' from Lesson 1 with puppet. Puppet introduces itself: 'Je m'appelle Pierre!'
opening.visualSupports: Point to self gesture for 'je', point to name tag for 'm'appelle', questioning gesture for 'comment'

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves se rappellent-ils des salutations de la leçon 1?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Construire sur leurs connaissances existantes avec confiance
decisionPoints.ifNo: Réviser brièvement 'Bonjour' avant d'introduire les noms

main.activity: Name introduction circle. Puppet asks 'Comment tu t'appelles?' to each child. Use name cards with photos. Practice pointing to self and saying/showing names.
materials: mirror for self-recognition (1 large or 5 small)
main.visualSupports: Point to self clearly, hold up name cards, use questioning facial expressions and hand gestures

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to attempt saying their names in French?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage verbal attempts with puppet support and pronunciation modeling
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on pointing to name cards and self-recognition activities with gestures

decisionPoints.question: How much repetition is needed for 'Je m'appelle' pattern?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Repeat pattern with multiple examples and slow pace, emphasize gestures
decisionPoints.ifNo: Move to interactive name games and recognition activities with varied practice

decisionPoints.question: Should we include family names or focus on first names only?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both first and family names for confident students
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on first names only to build confidence

closing.activity: Goodbye circle where puppet says 'Au revoir [name]!' to each child while they hold their name card.
closing.visualSupports: Point to name card, wave goodbye, use child's name with clear pronunciation

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves montrent-ils de la fierté à partager leurs noms en français?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Célébrer leur courage et leurs efforts d'apprentissage
decisionPoints.ifNo: Rassurer que tous les noms sont beaux en français

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students confused about name introduction pattern
troubleshooting.then: Use more visual name cards, practice with puppet first, focus on gestures before words

lessons.realWorldConnection: How introductions work in French families and communities

forStruggling: Use picture name cards with photos only
Allow pointing to self instead of verbal response
Practice 'Je m'appelle' with simple gestures first
Use mirror for self-recognition support
forAdvanced: Encourage full sentence 'Je m'appelle [first name] [last name]'
Practice asking 'Comment tu t'appelles?' to classmates
Help puppet introduce itself to other students
Add politeness words 's'il vous plaît'
forELL: Compare name introductions in home language
Use visual name sequence cards
Allow bilingual name explanations if needed
Focus on French pronunciation of their actual name
forIEP: Adapt communication method to individual needs
Use augmentative communication tools if available
Allow longer processing time for responses
Modify self-pointing gestures as needed

Demonstrates understanding of name introduction pattern
Participates in name circle activities positively

lessons.title: Les couleurs magiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize and respond to basic color words through visual objects and movement

opening.activity: Review greetings and names. Introduce color magic with colored scarves or fabric appearing from a box.
opening.visualSupports: Hold up colors clearly, use magic gestures, exaggerated surprise expressions

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves sont-ils fascinés par la magie des couleurs?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Utiliser plus de magie et de surprise pour introduire chaque couleur
decisionPoints.ifNo: Se concentrer sur la manipulation simple des objets colorés

main.activity: Color exploration stations: touch red objects, find blue items, dance with yellow scarves. Color matching games with large visual cards.
materials: colored objects - blocks, balls, crayons (25+ of each color)
main.visualSupports: Point clearly to colors, use searching gestures for finding activities, dancing movements for each color

decisionPoints.question: Which colors are students naturally drawn to?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Start with preferred colors and build confidence before introducing others
decisionPoints.ifNo: Introduce all three colors equally with multiple exposures and repetition

decisionPoints.question: Should we use more movement games or quiet observation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on active color games and dancing with scarves for kinesthetic learners
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use seated color sorting and matching activities for focused attention

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to attempt color names verbally?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage color name attempts while handling colored objects
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on color recognition through pointing and sorting activities

closing.activity: Color goodbye game: each child chooses a colored scarf and waves 'Au revoir rouge!' or their chosen color.
closing.visualSupports: Hold up chosen color clearly, exaggerated waving, color name pronunciation with lip reading support

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves peuvent-ils choisir et nommer leur couleur préférée?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourager le choix personnel et célébrer leurs préférences
decisionPoints.ifNo: Aider à choisir une couleur et accepter les gestes seulement

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty distinguishing color words
troubleshooting.then: Use more physical objects, slower repetition, focus on one color at a time with multiple examples

lessons.realWorldConnection: Describing the colorful world around us - flowers, toys, clothes

forStruggling: Start with one color only (rouge - most distinct)
Use larger colored objects for easier handling
Allow color matching instead of naming
Provide hand-over-hand support for sorting
forAdvanced: Add color combinations 'rouge et bleu'
Encourage describing objects 'une balle rouge'
Practice color questions 'Quelle couleur?'
Help demonstrate color activities for peers
forELL: Connect colors to home language equivalents
Use cultural color significance discussions
Allow bilingual color descriptions initially
Focus on visual color recognition first
forIEP: Adapt color materials for sensory needs
Use high contrast colors if visual needs exist
Modify movement activities as needed
Provide alternative color identification methods

observable: Student identifies rouge when shown red objects
Student responds to color words with appropriate pointing
Student participates in color movement activities
Student shows preference for certain colors and can indicate choice
checkpoints: Can match red objects to red objects
Shows recognition of 'rouge' when spoken

Demonstrates understanding that colors have French names

lessons.title: Mes premiers nombres
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize numbers 1-5 through finger counting, songs, and visual representations

opening.activity: Review colors with finger painting gesture. Introduce counting with Pierre puppet showing fingers for 'un, deux, trois'.
opening.visualSupports: Clear finger counting gestures, large number visuals, rhythmic counting movements

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves se souviennent-ils des couleurs pour les relier aux nombres?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Utiliser les objets colorés pour compter et connecter les apprentissages
decisionPoints.ifNo: Se concentrer uniquement sur les nombres avec les doigts

main.activity: Counting song with finger actions. Count colored objects from previous lesson. Number hop: hop once for 'un', twice for 'deux', three times for 'trois'.
materials: colored counting objects (75+ total - 25 each of red, blue, yellow)
number path on floor (1 large or 25 small)
main.visualSupports: Exaggerated finger counting, clear pointing to numbers, hopping movements with counting rhythm

decisionPoints.question: How are students responding to finger counting with French numbers?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Extend to more complex counting games and add 'quatre, cinq'
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple finger recognition and one-to-one correspondence with objects

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on listening or include some speaking?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage counting attempts with finger support and puppet modeling
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on recognition and finger counting responses without pressure to speak

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for movement-based counting activities?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Incorporate number hopping and counting while moving
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep counting activities seated with manipulatives and finger work

closing.activity: Counting goodbye: count three waves 'un, deux, trois' and say 'Au revoir!' Pierre puppet counts students.
closing.visualSupports: Clear finger counting for waves, visible number cards, rhythmic counting gestures

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves peuvent-ils compter avec leurs doigts et dire au revoir?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Célébrer leur capacité à compter en français
decisionPoints.ifNo: Aider à compter ensemble et accepter les gestes seulement

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students struggling with number-finger coordination
troubleshooting.then: Use larger visual number cards, practice finger counting slowly, focus on one number at a time

lessons.realWorldConnection: Counting everyday things - toys, books, fingers, age

Use large manipulatives for easier grasping
Allow pointing instead of finger counting
Provide one-on-one counting support

Practice counting backwards 'trois, deux, un'
Count different object types 'un crayon, deux crayons'

Use number cognates where available

lessons.title: Ma famille française
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand family words through photos, drawings, and inclusive family representations

opening.activity: Review counting fingers and colors. Pierre puppet shows family photos and introduces 'Ma famille!'
opening.visualSupports: Heart gesture for 'famille', pointing to family members, warm facial expressions

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves semblent-ils à l'aise de parler de leur famille?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourager le partage chaleureux et les connexions familiales
decisionPoints.ifNo: Se concentrer sur la famille de la marionnette pour commencer doucement

main.activity: Family photo sharing circle. Students can share photos or draw their families. Practice 'maman', 'papa', 'famille' with inclusive examples (two moms, single parent, grandparents, etc.).
main.visualSupports: Hugging gesture for family love, pointing to family members, inclusive visual examples

decisionPoints.question: How do we honor diverse family structures sensitively?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use inclusive examples and let children define their own families confidently
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on traditional examples but remain open to student sharing when comfortable

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to share about their families?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage sharing with puppet support and visual aids for comfort
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on listening and observing family examples with optional participation

decisionPoints.question: Should we emphasize drawing or photo sharing for family representation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on drawing activities to include all students regardless of photo availability
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use photo sharing for those who have them, provide drawing alternative

closing.activity: Family love circle: send hugs to our families and say 'Au revoir, famille!' with heart gestures.
closing.visualSupports: Heart gestures over heart, hugging motions, warm smiling expressions, gentle 'famille' pronunciation

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves peuvent-ils envoyer de l'amour à leurs familles en français?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Célébrer cette connexion émotionnelle et linguistique
decisionPoints.ifNo: Modéliser des gestes d'amour simples et accepter la participation silencieuse

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students emotional about family separation or differences
troubleshooting.then: Focus on love and connection, use puppet for comfort, validate all family structures

lessons.realWorldConnection: How French-speaking families talk about themselves and show love

Use simple family vocabulary 'maman, papa' only

Use cultural family traditions in discussions

Use alternative communication methods for family sharing

lessons.title: Les animaux amusants
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize animal names through sounds, movements, and visual supports

opening.activity: Review family words with Pierre puppet. Introduce animal friends: puppet meets a 'chat' with meowing and paw gestures.
materials: animal puppets or toys - cat, dog, bird (1 each)
opening.visualSupports: Cat paw gestures, dog panting and tail wagging movements, bird flying motions

main.activity: Animal movement game: crawl like 'chat', pant like 'chien', fly like 'oiseau'. Animal sound matching and movement imitation with visual cards.
materials: animal picture cards (25+ of each animal)
main.visualSupports: Clear animal movements, animal sound mimicking, pointing to animal features

decisionPoints.question: Which animal movements engage students most?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on preferred animals and extend movement activities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Try different animals or use more visual/auditory approaches

decisionPoints.question: Should we include animal sounds or focus on names?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Combine sounds with names for multi-sensory learning
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on visual recognition and movement only

closing.activity: Animal goodbye parade: each child chooses an animal movement and sound to say goodbye.
closing.visualSupports: Model animal movements clearly, encourage gentle movements, animal sound demonstrations

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelmed by animal movements or sounds
troubleshooting.then: Use quieter activities, focus on gentle animal gestures, use stuffed animals for comfort

lessons.realWorldConnection: Animals in our neighborhoods, farms, and French-speaking countries

lessons.title: Mes parties du corps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify basic body parts through songs, movements, and touching exercises

opening.activity: Review animal movements using our bodies. Pierre puppet touches his 'tête' and asks students to touch theirs.
opening.visualSupports: Clear touching gestures, pointing to body parts, exaggerated movements

main.activity: Body part song with actions: 'Tête, épaules, genoux et pieds' adapted for 'tête, main, pied'. Simon Says game with body parts. Mirror exploration touching named parts.
main.visualSupports: Touch head for 'tête', wave hands for 'main', stomp feet for 'pied', mirror reflection activities

decisionPoints.question: How comfortable are students with body part songs?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Extend to more complex body part games and sequences
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple touching and pointing activities

decisionPoints.question: Should we use mirrors or partner activities?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use mirrors for self-discovery and awareness
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use partner activities for social interaction

closing.activity: Body part goodbye: touch 'tête', wave 'main', stomp 'pied' and say 'Au revoir!'
closing.visualSupports: Clear body part demonstrations, gentle touching motions, rhythmic goodbye sequence

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students uncomfortable with body part touching or movements

lessons.realWorldConnection: Taking care of our bodies and describing ourselves to others

lessons.title: Les objets de classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize classroom objects through touch, pointing, and simple commands

opening.activity: Review body parts by using them to find classroom objects. Pierre puppet picks up a 'crayon' with his 'main'.
opening.visualSupports: Clear pointing to objects, holding and touching gestures, searching movements

main.activity: Classroom scavenger hunt: find and touch 'crayon', 'livre', 'table'. Object sorting game. Practice giving and receiving classroom objects with simple commands.
main.visualSupports: Point clearly to objects, demonstrate searching, show giving and receiving gestures

decisionPoints.question: Which classroom objects are most meaningful to students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on familiar, frequently used objects
decisionPoints.ifNo: Introduce variety and let students explore preferences

decisionPoints.question: Should we use scavenger hunts or direct instruction?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use active searching and discovery activities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use seated demonstration and object manipulation

closing.activity: Object appreciation circle: each child holds a classroom object and we say 'Merci, crayon!' or 'Au revoir, livre!'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students confused by similar-looking objects or commands

lessons.title: J'aime et je n'aime pas
lessons.oneGoal: Students will express simple preferences through gestures, facial expressions, and visual supports

opening.activity: Review classroom objects. Pierre puppet shows strong love for a 'livre' saying 'J'aime!' with heart gesture.
materials: variety of objects from previous lessons
opening.visualSupports: Heart gesture for 'j'aime', X or shaking head for 'non', thumbs up for 'oui'

main.activity: Preference exploration: show objects/pictures and let students show thumbs up/down. Practice 'J'aime' with heart gesture and 'Non' with gentle head shake. Choice-making activities.
main.visualSupports: Exaggerated facial expressions, clear thumbs up/down gestures, heart hugging for likes

decisionPoints.question: How are students showing preferences non-verbally?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Build on their natural expressions and gestures
decisionPoints.ifNo: Model clear preference expressions and give time to practice

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on positive expressions first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize 'j'aime' and positive choices initially
decisionPoints.ifNo: Show both positive and negative equally

closing.activity: Preference sharing circle: each child shows one thing they love with 'J'aime' gesture and heart.

troubleshooting.then: Focus on positive preferences first, use puppet to model, make choices less personal

lessons.title: Les actions quotidiennes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand basic action words through demonstration, mime, and physical response

opening.activity: Review preferences with movement: 'J'aime marcher!' Pierre puppet demonstrates walking, jumping, dancing.
opening.visualSupports: Clear walking steps, jumping movements, dancing gestures with rhythm

decisionPoints.question: Les élèves semblent-ils prêts pour les actions physiques?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourager les mouvements créatifs avec la musique
decisionPoints.ifNo: Commencer par des gestes assis et des actions plus douces

main.activity: Action station rotation: practice 'marcher' around the room, 'sauter' on mats, 'danser' to music. Action Simon Says game. Mime and guess activities.
materials: music for dancing (CD player or speaker)

decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on preferred actions and extend practice time
decisionPoints.ifNo: Try gentler versions or seated adaptations of actions

decisionPoints.question: Should we use more demonstration or student participation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage active student participation and leadership
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use more teacher/puppet demonstration with gradual participation

closing.activity: Action goodbye sequence: everyone 'marche' to the door, 'saute' twice, 'danse' and says 'Au revoir!'
closing.visualSupports: Gentle movement demonstrations, calming gestures, appreciation expressions for effort

lessons.title: Les saisons et météo
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize weather and season words through window observations, clothing, and sensory experiences

opening.activity: Review actions by 'marcher' to the window. Pierre puppet looks outside and comments on 'soleil' or 'pluie'.
opening.visualSupports: Point to sun/rain outside, sun gesture (arms up in circle), rain gesture (fingers falling down)

decisionPoints.question: La météo extérieure correspond-elle aux cartes d'apprentissage?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Utiliser la vraie météo comme outil d'enseignement principal

lessons.title: Notre célébration française
lessons.oneGoal: Students will celebrate their French learning journey through showcase activities, reflection, and community sharing (extension/enrichment)

opening.activity: Review musical joy. Pierre puppet announces it's time to 'célébrer' because everyone should feel 'fier' of their French learning!
materials: learning portfolio pictures (photos from all 20 lessons)
opening.visualSupports: Celebration gestures, proud expressions, achievement recognition motions

main.activity: Learning celebration showcase: students choose favorite activities from 20 lessons to demonstrate. French learning portfolio sharing. Celebration activities with all vocabulary. Community appreciation circle.
materials: portfolio materials (student work samples from unit)
showcase props from all lessons (puppet, cards, instruments, etc.)
camera for memories (tablet or phone for class photos)
main.visualSupports: Supportive celebration gestures, achievement recognition, community appreciation expressions

decisionPoints.question: How do we honor each student's unique learning journey?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Celebrate individual progress and different learning styles
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on group achievements and shared experiences

decisionPoints.question: Should celebration be classroom-focused or include families?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include families if possible for broader community celebration
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep celebration intimate and classroom-focused

closing.activity: Final celebration circle: each student shares one French word they love and we 'réussir' together with a big group hug!
closing.visualSupports: Proud celebration expressions, achievement recognition gestures, community appreciation movements

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students sad about ending or feeling they didn't learn enough
troubleshooting.then: Focus on continuation, celebrate all growth, emphasize ongoing French journey

lessons.realWorldConnection: Celebrating learning achievements builds confidence and motivation for continued language exploration

forStruggling: Allow celebration participation without performance pressure
Focus on individual growth rather than comparison to others
Provide visual reminders of their personal learning journey
Celebrate effort and participation over perfect French production
forAdvanced: Encourage leadership in celebration activities and helping others
Create detailed reflection on learning journey using French vocabulary
Help plan and lead parts of the celebration showcase
Connect learning to future French exploration goals
forELL: Celebrate bilingual learning journey and language growth
Allow celebration sharing in both home language and French
Connect French learning to overall language development pride
Honor cultural diversity within French learning celebration
forIEP: Adapt celebration participation to individual comfort and communication needs
Provide alternative ways to demonstrate learning and growth
Allow flexible participation in celebration activities
Focus on individual achievements and progress at personal pace

checkpoints: Can identify and share personal French learning growth and achievements

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: ""

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en français
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
Bonjour, mes amis!, Je m'appelle..., Les couleurs magiques, Mes premiers nombres, Ma famille française

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Il est normal et bénéfique que votre enfant mélange les langues à la maison.

N'hésitez pas à me contacter si vous avez des questions ou si vous souhaitez partager des ressources culturelles liées à cette unité.

Merci pour votre soutien continu dans l'apprentissage du français!

Cordialement,
[Nom de l'enseignant(e)]
